native_record.PROPERTY_NAME: Recovery closes on required function and state postconditions
native_record.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Repairable-system restoration, recovery blocks, high-availability operations, recovery-oriented computing and modern reconstitution guidance.
native_record.ORIGINAL_FORM: Count repair complete when the failed component is returned to an “up” state.
native_record.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Restart, failover or repair may leave stale/corrupt state, unavailable dependencies, insufficient capacity or the initiating common cause.
native_record.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Re-establish the ERM-P001 required function, authoritative state and dependency readiness within the declared restoration bound.
native_record.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Process starts but user/mission function is wrong, incomplete, too slow, unauthorised or vulnerable to immediate recurrence.
native_record.MECHANISM: Define recovery source/authority, reconcile state, verify dependencies/capacity, perform independent end-to-end functional checks and control return to service.
native_record.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Restart, retry, failover, rollback, restore, rebuild, repair, workaround or disaster recovery.
native_record.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For stateless, low-consequence functions, a direct end-to-end transaction after restart may be sufficient.
native_record.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Valid source, diagnosis/containment, state semantics, acceptance criteria, independent observability and fallback.
native_record.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
native_record.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
native_record.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
native_record.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.
native_record.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.
native_record.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
native_record.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents “green after restart” from being mistaken for restoration and reduces recurrent/corrupt recovery.
native_record.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Operator, incident commander, mission owner, user and return-to-service authority.
native_record.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Stale replica; incomplete replay; hidden dependency down; undercapacity; recurring trigger; invalid backup; monitor shares fault.
native_record.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Exhaustive post-recovery validation can delay urgent service; checks must be risk- and time-proportionate.
native_record.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Repair completion evolved from component-up to state-, dependency-, consumer- and mission-valid restoration.
native_record.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A recovery case with explicit preconditions, authoritative state, functional/data/dependency postconditions, independent validation and fallback.
native_record.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A closed incident or successful command is not the property; observed re-establishment of required function is.
native_record.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: GitLab lost data despite recovery work; AWS performed integrity safety checks before full service; Meta staged restoration under load (SRC-058–SRC-060).
native_record.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: For truly stateless/idempotent components, simple restart may be a valid cheap path—but that must be established, not assumed.
native_record.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What independent postcondition set is sufficient for complex services without making RTO unattainable?

current_claim.bearer: A recovery operation and a declared local or mission postcondition.
current_claim.proposition: Recovery success should be stated as the postcondition actually re-established, with unresolved external effects and dependencies separately retained.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: A command exit status is evidence only for its defined operation. A stronger functional claim needs checks adequate to that function; complete elimination of every latent cause is not required to establish a bounded restoration.
current_claim.model_domain: Postcondition satisfaction can be a logical/functional result. Future reliability and external reconciliation remain additional claims.
current_claim.mechanism: Restores useful state/function and checks the receiving criterion rather than equating procedure completion with success.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Resume a local operation, restore wider service, remain degraded, investigate or stop.
current_claim.positive_scope: Internal state restoration, partial service recovery and full mission return when each has adequate evidence.
current_claim.negative_scope: No blanket requirement for exhaustive validation, independent reviewers or global causal closure before any partial restoration counts.
current_claim.counterexample: C04's internal consistency holds while credentials and an external counterparty remain unavailable; both facts are preserved.
current_claim.criterion: State precondition, postcondition, observation oracle, residual effects, uncertainty and the scope of return-to-service authority.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Architecture/taxonomy and operator account; no restoration exercise on a deployed system was performed.
current_claim.remaining_premises: State authority, consistency, compatibility, valid oracle, relevant dependencies and accepted residual risk.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: For a simple stateless function, one direct transaction may establish the bounded claim; replace/rebuild may be cheaper than state repair.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Validation time can delay useful recovery. Choose checks that discriminate the asserted result and avoid mandatory unrelated controls.
current_claim.audit_question: Which postcondition is now true, what observation supports it, and which wider functions or irreversible effects remain unresolved?
current_claim.change_note: Scopes the native required-function closure to the claim actually made; independent validation is a risk-sensitive technique, not an unconditional ritual.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RECOVERY_ACTION: Restores useful state/function and checks the receiving criterion rather than equating procedure completion with success.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS: Verify dependencies that the particular restoration claim requires. Record unverified external dependencies separately; they prevent an unsupported wider completion claim but do not erase a valid internal postcondition.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.VALIDATION: An observation or proof adequate to the named functional/state postcondition. Independent end-to-end checks are appropriate when the claim needs them, not a universal prerequisite for every local deterministic restoration.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY: Keep proof of the postcondition separate from actual permission to resume consequential service. Name the relevant decision maker or rule when applicable.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK: A justified bounded fallback where it adds protection. It need not resolve every root cause, and not every restoration claim requires a second full recovery mechanism.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Recovery success should be stated as the postcondition actually re-established, with unresolved external effects and dependencies separately retained. Guard: A command exit status is evidence only for its defined operation. A stronger functional claim needs checks adequate to that function; complete elimination of every latent cause is not required to establish a bounded restoration.

native_audit_unique.POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY: Restoration speed versus diagnostic confidence, state correctness and evidence preservation.
native_audit_unique.QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT:
- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate recovery closes on required function and state postconditions?
- Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version?
- Which enumerated failures can the diagnostic detect and isolate within the required latency, and what are the false-positive and false-negative costs?
- Does recovery close on independently checked required function, state and dependency postconditions rather than process restart or procedure completion?

current_audit_questions: Which postcondition is now true, what observation supports it, and which wider functions or irreversible effects remain unresolved?
Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?
What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

native_record.PROPERTY_NAME: Backup, restore and reconstitution paths must be exercised and validated
native_record.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Data backup/contingency practice, disaster recovery and current NIST restore/reconstitution guidance.
native_record.ORIGINAL_FORM: Maintain a backup copy and a recovery plan.
native_record.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Copies can be absent, stale, corrupt, inaccessible, incompatible, contaminated or impossible to restore within field constraints.
native_record.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Restore required data/state and application function to a trusted, current-enough configuration within RPO/RTO and consequence limits.
native_record.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Backup job reports success but restore cannot complete, recovered data is inconsistent, required tools/docs are unavailable or the same cause contaminates sources.
native_record.MECHANISM: Inventory sources, isolate/protect them, verify integrity/freshness, rehearse non-production restore, validate application semantics and reconstitution logistics.
native_record.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any claim of backup, disaster recovery, spare image, replicated state, rebuild-from-code or clean-room recovery.
native_record.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For reproducible stateless artefacts, verify rebuild and one functional check instead of elaborate backup infrastructure.
native_record.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Configuration manifests, credentials, tools, dependencies, capacity, state consistency, acceptance criteria and staff capability.
native_record.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
native_record.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
native_record.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
native_record.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
native_record.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.
native_record.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.
native_record.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Converts backup existence into demonstrated recoverability and exposes hidden RPO/RTO/support gaps.
native_record.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Service/data owner, operator, mission continuity authority and affected users.
native_record.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Silent backup failure; restore never tested; missing encryption key; version mismatch; partial database; dependent identity/DNS unavailable; contaminated image.
native_record.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Frequent full rehearsals are costly and can create production risk; representative, isolated exercises and cheaper checks should be chosen by decision value.
native_record.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Backup media inventory evolved toward recurring restore, application/state validation, clean reconstitution and dependency/tool readiness.
native_record.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A periodically refreshed restore/reconstitution demonstration closing on functional and state postconditions for the current configuration.
native_record.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A backup icon, policy or DR document is not the property; a valid exercised recovery path is.
native_record.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: GitLab’s periodic backups were not working and snapshots were unavailable; data could not be fully recovered (SRC-060).
native_record.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: A single successful restore does not establish all future restores, configurations or correlated disaster conditions.
native_record.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can restore evidence be maintained continuously for large stateful systems without prohibitive duplication?

native_record.DISPOSITION_RATIONALE: Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

current_claim.bearer: A backup/rebuild/reconstitution path with state, tools, permissions and a receiving function.
current_claim.proposition: Possessing a backup does not establish restore capability. A claimed path needs evidence that the required state and function can be reconstituted under the relevant configuration and resource assumptions.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: Exercise or other adequate evidence should cover the actual claim; refresh is triggered by material changes, stale assumptions or a binding obligation, not by an arbitrary universal frequency.
current_claim.model_domain: A restoration demonstration establishes the tested path and configuration. It does not establish success under every loss scenario.
current_claim.mechanism: Challenges accessibility, integrity, compatibility, missing authority and integration before relying on recovery.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Keep/modify a backup plan, replace it with rebuild, accept loss or schedule a proportionate exercise.
current_claim.positive_scope: Isolated tests, existing valid demonstrations and cheap deterministic rebuild checks where sufficient.
current_claim.negative_scope: No production disruption or recurring full rehearsal quota follows from this research.
current_claim.counterexample: Readable backup bytes cannot restore service when the only decryption credential was lost with the original system.
current_claim.criterion: Trace what is recoverable, under which loss, how long and with which residual data loss; identify evidence invalidators.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Scoped current NIST guidance and technical/incident mechanisms; no independent efficacy trial or actual restoration conducted.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Backup trust, state currency, resource availability, protected authority, dependencies and realistic load.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: Recreate reproducible stateless artifacts and perform one functional check; use existing current evidence when new testing adds no discrimination.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Account for storage, credentials, exercise disruption, staff and obsolete formats; retire redundant paths only after protecting remaining obligations.
current_claim.audit_question: Which specific loss can this path recover from, what evidence exists, and which change would invalidate it?
current_claim.change_note: Preserves the native anti-backup-theater claim while replacing unconditional periodicity with meaningful freshness and applicable obligations.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS: Verify dependencies that the particular restoration claim requires. Record unverified external dependencies separately; they prevent an unsupported wider completion claim but do not erase a valid internal postcondition.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.VALIDATION: An observation or proof adequate to the named functional/state postcondition. Independent end-to-end checks are appropriate when the claim needs them, not a universal prerequisite for every local deterministic restoration.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK: A justified bounded fallback where it adds protection. It need not resolve every root cause, and not every restoration claim requires a second full recovery mechanism.

A claimed path needs evidence that the required state and function can be reconstituted under the relevant configuration and resource assumptions. RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CLAIM: Possessing a backup does not establish restore capability. A claimed path needs evidence that the required state and function can be reconstituted under the relevant configuration and resource assumptions. Guard: Exercise or other adequate evidence should cover the actual claim; refresh is triggered by material changes, stale assumptions or a binding obligation, not by an arbitrary universal frequency.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR: Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Identify the hardware, software, data, model, environment, dependency and procedure conditions that the particular claim materially depends on. An exhaustive live inventory is not universally required.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE: Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN: Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. Retrospective observations retain their actual design limits.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MODEL: Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.ASSUMPTIONS: Declare the assumptions actually used, such as independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage or representativeness. Their absence from an unrelated deterministic claim is not automatically a defect.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY: Express uncertainty appropriate to the claim. A stochastic estimate needs its model and uncertainty; an exact deterministic result need not invent a probability interval. A qualitative criterion may remain qualitative.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS: Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.COVERAGE: Empirical inference is limited by the observed population and design; a mathematical or exhaustive finite result can cover its explicitly proved domain. Neither automatically supplies external-system correspondence.

A claimed path needs evidence that the required state and function can be reconstituted under the relevant configuration and resource assumptions. Guard: Exercise or other adequate evidence should cover the actual claim; refresh is triggered by material changes, stale assumptions or a binding obligation, not by an arbitrary universal frequency.

properties.profile_scope: The native applicability classification is retained for this candidate claim. Applicable templates describe claim-specific questions, not a mandatory bundle for every system. Nonapplicable reasons remain exact.

HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Historical attribution retained, with current typed genealogy and exact fresh scopes. No original executed-prompt or earliest-priority inference.

FORMAL_OR_PROBABILISTIC_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: A restoration demonstration establishes the tested path and configuration. It does not establish success under every loss scenario. Scoped current NIST guidance and technical/incident mechanisms; no independent efficacy trial or actual restoration conducted.

LIFE_DATA_OR_FIELD_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Selected reported operating/experimental evidence, if listed; no new empirical dataset received or reanalyzed. Empty list means no such fresh direct evidence assigned to this claim.

DEMONSTRATION_TEST_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Author cases are constructed arithmetic/logical witnesses only. No deployed demonstration or physical/operational test was performed.

INCIDENT_OR_FAILURE_CASE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Listed operator incident accounts support reported mechanisms at those events, not prevalence or independently verified countermeasure effects.

OPERATIONAL_PRACTICE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Listed normative/practitioner/owner sources explain selected mechanisms, intent or currentness at their access scopes; they are not independent causal efficacy studies.

REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: No independent replication of the author cases or target field effect. Related source versions, chapters and reports are grouped in the source dependence register.

TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: No target-system transfer established. Backup trust, state currency, resource availability, protected authority, dependencies and realistic load.

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.current_scope_judgment: Exercise or other adequate evidence should cover the actual claim; refresh is triggered by material changes, stale assumptions or a binding obligation, not by an arbitrary universal frequency. No production disruption or recurring full rehearsal quota follows from this research.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Readable backup bytes cannot restore service when the only decryption credential was lost with the original system. Scoped current NIST guidance and technical/incident mechanisms; no independent efficacy trial or actual restoration conducted.

native_audit_unique.POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY: Fast restoration versus backup integrity, freshness and reconstitution validation.
native_audit_unique.QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT:
- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate backup, restore and reconstitution paths must be exercised and validated?
- Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version?
- Does recovery close on independently checked required function, state and dependency postconditions rather than process restart or procedure completion?
- What population, denominator, model, confidence, censoring rule and expiry condition bound the reliability claim?

current_audit_questions: Which specific loss can this path recover from, what evidence exists, and which change would invalidate it?
Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?
What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

properties.current_name: Conditional validity of retry, restart, rollback and checkpoint recovery

native_record.PROPERTY_NAME: Conditional validity of retry, restart, rollback and checkpoint recovery
native_record.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Recovery blocks, checkpoint/restart, transaction rollback and high-availability operations.
native_record.ORIGINAL_FORM: Retry a failed operation, restart the process, roll back the version or resume from a checkpoint.
native_record.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Recovery primitives are beneficial for transient/local faults but amplify overload, repeat deterministic faults or restore inconsistent state when assumptions fail.
native_record.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Complete the intended operation or restore service/state without duplicate side effects, overload, corruption or recurrence.
native_record.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Retry storm, non-idempotent duplicate, domino rollback, stale checkpoint, incompatible rollback, restart loop or hidden dependency failure.
native_record.MECHANISM: Classify fault transience; bound retries/backoff; establish idempotency; coordinate checkpoints; validate rollback compatibility; circuit-break and escalate.
native_record.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Transient faults, process crashes, failed releases or recoverable state loss where operation semantics and state are known.
native_record.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Do not retry deterministic validation errors or overload; fail clearly and preserve evidence.
native_record.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Idempotency/deduplication, state consistency, checkpoint freshness, dependency capacity, rollback artefacts and stop conditions.
native_record.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
native_record.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
native_record.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: Credible failure-domain independence, common-cause analysis, standby condition, switchover coverage and state compatibility.
native_record.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
native_record.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.
native_record.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
native_record.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Shortens restoration for the subset of failures these primitives actually cover.
native_record.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Service owner, operator, recovery controller and users.
native_record.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Retries increase load; checkpoint overhead; uncoordinated state; old schema cannot roll back; automated loop destroys evidence.
native_record.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Recovery primitives can mask design defects and create correlated cascades; their success rate is workload- and fault-specific.
native_record.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Unconditional restart evolved toward bounded, idempotent, state-aware recovery with escalation and postcondition validation.
native_record.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A fault-class-specific recovery policy with bounded attempts, consistency/compatibility proof, load protection, observation and fallback.
native_record.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A restart button, retry library or checkpoint file is not the property; valid semantics and successful postconditions are.
native_record.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: AWS accumulated backlogs and staged recovery; Meta avoided all-at-once restart; GitLab’s restore source was incomplete (SRC-058–SRC-060).
native_record.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: For independent transient faults in stateless/idempotent operations, retry/restart has strong practical value.
native_record.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should automated recovery estimate when a fault is transient versus systematic under sparse evidence?

native_record.DISPOSITION_RATIONALE: Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

current_claim.bearer: A retry, restart, rollback, failover or checkpoint mechanism for a specified fault class.
current_claim.proposition: Recovery primitives work under different guards; their local success does not establish that external side effects are undone or that repeated attempts remain beneficial under load.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: A retry needs a recoverable failure and acceptable repeat semantics; rollback needs a compatible retained state; checkpoint restart needs enough recoverable state and handling of external effects. Guard each mechanism independently.
current_claim.model_domain: An algorithm's state transition can be verified at its abstraction boundary; infrastructure capacity, irreversible actions and external contracts remain separate.
current_claim.mechanism: Changes execution state, input timing or chosen alternative to escape a fault manifestation.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Retry, switch algorithm/path, restart, roll back, repair forward or fail clearly.
current_claim.positive_scope: Bounded automatic/manual recovery and partial internal restoration without root-cause knowledge.
current_claim.negative_scope: No universal no-retry-on-overload theorem: a controlled later attempt can be useful after load changes. Unbounded immediate retries during overload can worsen it.
current_claim.counterexample: C10raises90arrivals/s to108attempts/s against100capacity; C14's weak acceptance check can accept a wrong result; C04retains external failure.
current_claim.criterion: Name the fault, state boundary, repeat/rollback semantics, resource effect, failure of the recovery mechanism and fallback.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Primary historical mechanisms, operator report and model arithmetic; historical Gray recommendations are not current operational/security policy.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Idempotence or deduplication, valid saved state, compatibility, current capacity, time limits and consumer acceptance.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: One transparent failure, replacement or manual repair can be better than automatic repeated work.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Recovery logic increases complexity, load and diagnostic masking; retire retries or fallbacks whose rescue set no longer justifies them.
current_claim.audit_question: What particular failure can this primitive recover from, which effects cannot be reversed, and can its own attempts amplify the failure?
current_claim.change_note: Retains native conditionality and qualifies an overly literal no-retry-on-overload reading.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Conditional validity of retry, restart, rollback and checkpoint recovery
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.INITIATING_FAILURE: Retry storm, non-idempotent duplicate, domino rollback, stale checkpoint, incompatible rollback, restart loop or hidden dependency failure. Current limitation: No universal no-retry-on-overload theorem: a controlled later attempt can be useful after load changes. Unbounded immediate retries during overload can worsen it.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RECOVERY_ACTION: Changes execution state, input timing or chosen alternative to escape a fault manifestation.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.AUTHORITY_SOURCE: State/configuration identity and the actual authority relevant to the action or claim. A pure model has no external action authority; a bounded internal restore does not by itself establish authority to resume a wider service.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.CHECKPOINT_BACKUP_SPARE_OR_ALTERNATE: Declared checkpoint, replica, backup, spare, rebuild source or manual workaround.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RPO_OR_STATE_LOSS_BOUND: State/data loss bound where the function depends on preserved state; explicitly state a nontrigger for stateless or directly reconstructible functions.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND: The declared restoration interval or bound, if the claim requires one. Distinguish detection, waiting, logistics, repair and validation and avoid summing overlapping intervals.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.STATE_RECONCILIATION: Reconcile the state required by the named restored function. Broader divergent or external state may remain an explicit residual; authoritative wider service requires its own relevant conditions.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS: Complete the intended operation or restore service/state without duplicate side effects, overload, corruption or recurrence. Current scope: Bounded automatic/manual recovery and partial internal restoration without root-cause knowledge.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS: Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS: Verify dependencies that the particular restoration claim requires. Record unverified external dependencies separately; they prevent an unsupported wider completion claim but do not erase a valid internal postcondition.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.VALIDATION: An observation or proof adequate to the named functional/state postcondition. Independent end-to-end checks are appropriate when the claim needs them, not a universal prerequisite for every local deterministic restoration.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY: Keep proof of the postcondition separate from actual permission to resume consequential service. Name the relevant decision maker or rule when applicable.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK: A justified bounded fallback where it adds protection. It need not resolve every root cause, and not every restoration claim requires a second full recovery mechanism.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Recovery primitives work under different guards; their local success does not establish that external side effects are undone or that repeated attempts remain beneficial under load. Guard: A retry needs a recoverable failure and acceptable repeat semantics; rollback needs a compatible retained state; checkpoint restart needs enough recoverable state and handling of external effects. Guard each mechanism independently.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.REASON: The property is primarily a design/operation mechanism; its validation still follows ERM-P026–P029.

properties.profile_scope: The native applicability classification is retained for this candidate claim. Applicable templates describe claim-specific questions, not a mandatory bundle for every system. Nonapplicable reasons remain exact.

HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Historical attribution retained, with current typed genealogy and exact fresh scopes. No original executed-prompt or earliest-priority inference.

FORMAL_OR_PROBABILISTIC_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: An algorithm's state transition can be verified at its abstraction boundary; infrastructure capacity, irreversible actions and external contracts remain separate. Primary historical mechanisms, operator report and model arithmetic; historical Gray recommendations are not current operational/security policy.

LIFE_DATA_OR_FIELD_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Selected reported operating/experimental evidence, if listed; no new empirical dataset received or reanalyzed. Empty list means no such fresh direct evidence assigned to this claim.

DEMONSTRATION_TEST_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Author cases are constructed arithmetic/logical witnesses only. No deployed demonstration or physical/operational test was performed.

INCIDENT_OR_FAILURE_CASE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Listed operator incident accounts support reported mechanisms at those events, not prevalence or independently verified countermeasure effects.

OPERATIONAL_PRACTICE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Listed normative/practitioner/owner sources explain selected mechanisms, intent or currentness at their access scopes; they are not independent causal efficacy studies.

REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: No independent replication of the author cases or target field effect. Related source versions, chapters and reports are grouped in the source dependence register.

TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: No target-system transfer established. Idempotence or deduplication, valid saved state, compatibility, current capacity, time limits and consumer acceptance.

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.current_scope_judgment: A retry needs a recoverable failure and acceptable repeat semantics; rollback needs a compatible retained state; checkpoint restart needs enough recoverable state and handling of external effects. Guard each mechanism independently. No universal no-retry-on-overload theorem: a controlled later attempt can be useful after load changes. Unbounded immediate retries during overload can worsen it.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: C10raises90arrivals/s to108attempts/s against100capacity; C14's weak acceptance check can accept a wrong result; C04retains external failure. Primary historical mechanisms, operator report and model arithmetic; historical Gray recommendations are not current operational/security policy.

native_audit_unique.POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY: Rapid retry/restart versus overload, duplicate effects and corrupt-state recurrence.
native_audit_unique.QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT:
- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate conditional validity of retry, restart, rollback and checkpoint recovery?
- Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version?
- Are the supposed redundant channels actually separate failure domains, and is detection, switchover, state transfer and degraded capacity covered?
- Does recovery close on independently checked required function, state and dependency postconditions rather than process restart or procedure completion?

current_audit_questions: What particular failure can this primitive recover from, which effects cannot be reversed, and can its own attempts amplify the failure?
Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?
What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

properties.current_name: Repairability and maintainability by design

native_record.PROPERTY_NAME: Repairability and maintainability by design
native_record.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Post-war maintainability programmes, maintainability prediction/demonstration and modular field replacement.
native_record.ORIGINAL_FORM: Reduce mean corrective maintenance time through modularity, accessibility and standard repair tasks.
native_record.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A reliable design can impose unacceptable downtime or recurring error because faults cannot be isolated, accessed, repaired or verified in the field.
native_record.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Restore the defined function safely within the total downtime bound under actual field support conditions.
native_record.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Procedure exists but access, isolation, tools, spares, skills, state/configuration transfer or verification make repair infeasible or error-prone.
native_record.MECHANISM: Design for access, isolation, modular replacement, test points, diagnostics, standard interfaces, safe handling, configuration/state transfer and repair verification.
native_record.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Repairable/high-value/long-life systems, remote sites, tight restoration bounds, repeated service intervention or obsolescence exposure.
native_record.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For low-cost short-life items, replacement or graceful discard may dominate elaborate repairability.
native_record.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Maintenance concept, field observations, human factors, logistics, tools, documentation, configuration control and testability.
native_record.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
native_record.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
native_record.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
native_record.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.
native_record.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.
native_record.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.
native_record.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces active repair and error while making reliability growth and lifecycle support feasible.
native_record.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Maintainer, operator, logistics owner, asset owner and service user.
native_record.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Modularity moves complexity to interfaces; inaccessible fasteners; ambiguous connectors; replacement loses calibration/state; “no fault found.”
native_record.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Optimising predicted MTTR can ignore diagnosis, logistics and validation; modularity can add failure points.
native_record.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Task-time prediction evolved toward maintainability-by-design, testability, software operability, remote support and total restoration burden.
native_record.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Field-demonstrated restoration capability spanning detection, access, repair/replacement, configuration/state preservation, validation and return to service.
native_record.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A maintainability prediction is not the property; repair performed correctly under real support constraints is.
native_record.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Meta’s need for physical onsite access and GitLab’s undocumented/manual repair path show design and organisational support dominate restoration (SRC-059, SRC-060).
native_record.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: For disposable or non-repairable items, maintainability may not trigger; replacement/logistics still require analysis.
native_record.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can software state/configuration portability be treated as a first-class maintainability attribute across generations?

current_claim.bearer: The maintainability of an item under stated access, procedure, skill and resource conditions.
current_claim.proposition: Design can make diagnosis, access, repair/replacement and validation easier, but predicted or intrinsic maintainability is distinct from demonstrated restoration by an actual support organization.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: Bind a repair-time or effort claim to the task, configuration, environment, tools and personnel conditions. Modularity is useful only when its restoration benefit exceeds added interfaces and burden.
current_claim.model_domain: A design-level task decomposition is a proposal; measured time distributions require representative maintenance observations.
current_claim.mechanism: Access, replaceable boundaries, testability and retained state reduce selected restoration tasks or uncertainty.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Repair versus replace, interface design, service tooling, training or graceful discard.
current_claim.positive_scope: Designed repairability, bounded local demonstrations and actual field capability as separately labelled levels.
current_claim.negative_scope: No universal claim that modularity or automation shortens total downtime; no inferred human competence from a procedure.
current_claim.counterexample: A module swaps in minutes but diagnosis, credential acquisition and validation dominate the outage; added connectors create failures absent in a simpler sealed item.
current_claim.criterion: Compare the complete restoration task and its uncertainties, including maintenance-induced faults, under the stated resources.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Current publisher scope, primary maintenance guidance and historical operating account; paid IEC clauses and a new maintainability trial are not claimed.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Physical/software access, real skills/tools, compatibility, diagnosis and post-repair observations.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: Replacement, graceful discard or a simple known repair can dominate elaborate modularity for low-cost/short-life items.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Count interface failures, spares, documentation, training and obsolescence over the life cycle.
current_claim.audit_question: Is this a design promise or demonstrated support capability, and which tasks and conditions determine the full restoration burden?
current_claim.change_note: Separates native field-demonstrated mature form from valid but weaker design-level evidence instead of rejecting either.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS: Restore the defined function safely within the total downtime bound under actual field support conditions. Current scope: Designed repairability, bounded local demonstrations and actual field capability as separately labelled levels.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS: Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS: Verify dependencies that the particular restoration claim requires. Record unverified external dependencies separately; they prevent an unsupported wider completion claim but do not erase a valid internal postcondition.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.VALIDATION: An observation or proof adequate to the named functional/state postcondition. Independent end-to-end checks are appropriate when the claim needs them, not a universal prerequisite for every local deterministic restoration.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY: Keep proof of the postcondition separate from actual permission to resume consequential service. Name the relevant decision maker or rule when applicable.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK: A justified bounded fallback where it adds protection. It need not resolve every root cause, and not every restoration claim requires a second full recovery mechanism.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Design can make diagnosis, access, repair/replacement and validation easier, but predicted or intrinsic maintainability is distinct from demonstrated restoration by an actual support organization. Guard: Bind a repair-time or effort claim to the task, configuration, environment, tools and personnel conditions. Modularity is useful only when its restoration benefit exceeds added interfaces and burden.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.REASON: The property is primarily a design/operation mechanism; its validation still follows ERM-P026–P029.

properties.profile_scope: The native applicability classification is retained for this candidate claim. Applicable templates describe claim-specific questions, not a mandatory bundle for every system. Nonapplicable reasons remain exact.

HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Historical attribution retained, with current typed genealogy and exact fresh scopes. No original executed-prompt or earliest-priority inference.

FORMAL_OR_PROBABILISTIC_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: A design-level task decomposition is a proposal; measured time distributions require representative maintenance observations. Current publisher scope, primary maintenance guidance and historical operating account; paid IEC clauses and a new maintainability trial are not claimed.

LIFE_DATA_OR_FIELD_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Selected reported operating/experimental evidence, if listed; no new empirical dataset received or reanalyzed. Empty list means no such fresh direct evidence assigned to this claim.

DEMONSTRATION_TEST_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Author cases are constructed arithmetic/logical witnesses only. No deployed demonstration or physical/operational test was performed.

INCIDENT_OR_FAILURE_CASE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Listed operator incident accounts support reported mechanisms at those events, not prevalence or independently verified countermeasure effects.

OPERATIONAL_PRACTICE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Listed normative/practitioner/owner sources explain selected mechanisms, intent or currentness at their access scopes; they are not independent causal efficacy studies.

REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: No independent replication of the author cases or target field effect. Related source versions, chapters and reports are grouped in the source dependence register.

TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: No target-system transfer established. Physical/software access, real skills/tools, compatibility, diagnosis and post-repair observations.

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.current_scope_judgment: Bind a repair-time or effort claim to the task, configuration, environment, tools and personnel conditions. Modularity is useful only when its restoration benefit exceeds added interfaces and burden. No universal claim that modularity or automation shortens total downtime; no inferred human competence from a procedure.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: A module swaps in minutes but diagnosis, credential acquisition and validation dominate the outage; added connectors create failures absent in a simpler sealed item. Current publisher scope, primary maintenance guidance and historical operating account; paid IEC clauses and a new maintainability trial are not claimed.

native_audit_unique.QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT:
- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate repairability and maintainability by design?
- Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version?
- Which enumerated failures can the diagnostic detect and isolate within the required latency, and what are the false-positive and false-negative costs?
- Does recovery close on independently checked required function, state and dependency postconditions rather than process restart or procedure completion?

Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?
What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

properties.current_name: Supportability, logistics and operational maintenance capability

native_record.PROPERTY_NAME: Supportability, logistics and operational maintenance capability
native_record.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Integrated logistics support, operational availability and current IEC supportability practice.
native_record.ORIGINAL_FORM: Provision spares, tools, manuals, trained maintainers and maintenance facilities to meet downtime targets.
native_record.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A maintainable design remains unavailable because diagnosis, administration, transport, spares, credentials, tools, documentation or personnel are delayed.
native_record.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: The complete support system restores required function within the operational downtime bound across deployed locations and mission conditions.
native_record.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Low bench repair time is overwhelmed by waiting, access, approval, supplier lead time, obsolete parts, unavailable expertise or incompatible configuration.
native_record.MECHANISM: Model and measure total downtime; provision/position resources; exercise escalation; manage obsolescence; sustain documentation, credentials and skills.
native_record.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Distributed fleets, remote/contested sites, long-life assets, supplier concentration, strict availability or disaster recovery.
native_record.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For low-criticality items, accept longer restoration or stock simple replacements rather than build a complex support network.
native_record.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Demand rates, repair-level policy, supply data, workforce readiness, transport/access, contracts, configuration and obsolescence monitoring.
native_record.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
native_record.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
native_record.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
native_record.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
native_record.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.
native_record.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.
native_record.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Aligns achieved/operational availability with real support conditions rather than inherent design promises.
native_record.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Fleet/asset owner, logistics organisation, operator, maintainer and mission planner.
native_record.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Paper spares; wrong revision; expired credentials; inaccessible facility; unsupported dependency; concentrated specialist; supply disruption.
native_record.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Stocking and spare capacity are costly; forecasts are uncertain; overprovisioning can create obsolescence and maintenance burden.
native_record.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Spares provisioning broadened to lifecycle supportability, digital/software dependencies, remote operations and obsolescence management.
native_record.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A tested support concept with total-downtime data, resource/configuration identity, alternatives and explicit risk acceptance for uncovered sites/times.
native_record.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A logistics plan or SLA is not the property; actual timely access to the right resources is.
native_record.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Meta’s secure physical access delayed repair; GitLab relied on slower infrastructure in another region; both show logistics/access are reliability mechanisms (SRC-059, SRC-060).
native_record.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: High reliability or local repairability can reduce support demand, but does not eliminate the need to validate residual support assumptions.
native_record.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should supply-chain and workforce correlation be integrated with traditional stochastic availability models?

current_claim.bearer: A support system supplying maintenance capability at specified sites and times.
current_claim.proposition: Restoration depends on available people, spares, tools, information and authority as well as the item's repairability; the scope of supported operation must state those resource conditions.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: For the asserted mission/site/time, examine whether required resources can arrive and act within the needed window. Do not infer capability from staffing counts or policy existence.
current_claim.model_domain: Resource availability and scheduling may be modeled; actual access, competence and logistics need observations.
current_claim.mechanism: Reduces waiting and coordination delays or provides a substitute repair/rebuild path.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Stock a spare, arrange support, accept longer downtime or reduce the protected mission.
current_claim.positive_scope: Local resource inventories and tested support paths, including bounded manual alternatives.
current_claim.negative_scope: No universal overprovisioning target or requirement for an elaborate support network.
current_claim.counterexample: A technically repairable system remains unavailable because the sole specialist, spare, tool license or recovery credential is absent.
current_claim.criterion: Distinguish active repair from waiting, diagnose overlapping intervals, and identify which shortages can block the receiving function.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Scoped normative guidance and historical evidence; no staffing productivity, fatigue or agent performance was measured.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Site/time coverage, shared-demand correlation, inventory quality, authority and restoration validation.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: A cheap replacement, an accepted restoration delay or a smaller supported scope may be adequate.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Inventory ages, trained staff turn over and support itself needs maintenance; remove obsolete stock/support duties deliberately.
current_claim.audit_question: Which resource can become the restoration bottleneck, over what sites/times, and what happens when several failures demand it together?
current_claim.change_note: Retains native supportability while preventing paper support concepts from earning operational capability.

- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate supportability, logistics and operational maintenance capability?

properties.current_name: Maintenance-induced failure and maintenance human factors as system mechanisms

native_record.PROPERTY_NAME: Maintenance-induced failure and maintenance human factors as system mechanisms
native_record.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Field maintenance experience, RCM, human-factors programmes and common-cause analysis.
native_record.ORIGINAL_FORM: Record maintenance error as a cause category and improve procedures/training.
native_record.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Inspection, calibration, replacement, access, configuration or repair can introduce faults, disable redundancy or create shared misconfiguration.
native_record.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Maintenance must preserve or restore the required function without creating a new latent, common-cause or interface failure.
native_record.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Wrong part/configuration, omitted step, damage during access, common calibration error, simultaneous channel disablement or ineffective verification.
native_record.MECHANISM: Design out error opportunities; control configuration; isolate channels; use usable procedures/tools; manage fatigue/communication; verify function after work; learn without individual blame substitution.
native_record.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Intrusive maintenance, repeated “no fault found,” common-channel work, difficult access, night/remote work, complex software/configuration changes.
native_record.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Eliminate unnecessary maintenance or replace a fragile manual step with a simple poka-yoke/functional check where that is safer.
native_record.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Work-as-done observation, maintainability design, staffing/fatigue controls, independent verification, event reporting and organisational learning.
native_record.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
native_record.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
native_record.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
native_record.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.
native_record.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
native_record.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.
native_record.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces recurrence, common-cause exposure and downtime produced by the maintenance system itself.
native_record.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Maintainer, operator, fleet/service owner and mission authority.
native_record.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Blame-only investigation; unreadable procedures; undocumented workaround; verifier shares same misconception; work performed on both redundant channels.
native_record.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: “Human error” can become a residual label that hides design and organisational causes; added checks can create workload and new failure modes.
native_record.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Person-centred error counting evolved toward design-for-maintenance, organisational conditions, independent verification and work-as-done evidence.
native_record.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Maintenance treated as an operational mode with its own hazards, dependencies, state transitions, common-cause controls and post-maintenance functional proof.
native_record.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A sign-off or training record is not the property; reduced error opportunity and verified post-work function are.
native_record.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: AWS’s event began with an authorised maintenance command whose input removed excess capacity; GitLab’s recovery work accidentally removed the primary data directory (SRC-058, SRC-060).
native_record.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Some maintenance errors are genuinely individual slips, but durable control still requires analysing the conditions and barriers around them.
native_record.OPEN_QUESTIONS: Which post-maintenance checks best detect semantic/configuration errors without duplicating the entire mission test?

current_claim.bearer: A maintenance/change activity, its technical interfaces and human organizational conditions.
current_claim.proposition: Maintenance can introduce failures as well as remove them; human actions should be examined as part of the system mechanism rather than used as an unexplained blame category.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: For a maintenance task, examine misdiagnosis, access, sequencing, tools, permissions and post-change effects. Claims about workload or competence require actual human evidence.
current_claim.model_domain: A task hazard model identifies possibilities; attribution and frequency require observation and alternative explanations.
current_claim.mechanism: Changes state or components, sometimes creating shared faults, incorrect configuration or delayed latent failures.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Simplify or remove an intervention, improve access/error resistance, stage a change or check the resulting function.
current_claim.positive_scope: Mechanism-focused maintenance analysis and proportionate post-maintenance checks.
current_claim.negative_scope: No inference that an operator mention proves sole causation, that automation eliminates error, or that human findings measure machine-agent behavior.
current_claim.counterexample: A common update applied to many healthy systems introduces the same fault; additional manual checks can themselves increase interruption and workload.
current_claim.criterion: Distinguish action, context, causal hypothesis and observed outcome; test whether removing or simplifying the task protects the function.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Gray's selected historical operating data, one supplier incident account and current owner programme summaries; no new human study or independent causal attribution.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Task exposure, reporting completeness, actual working conditions, alternatives and residual responsibility.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: Remove unnecessary maintenance or use a simple fixture/direct functional check where it addresses the mechanism.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Account for fatigue, interruption, training and added checking burden without fabricating effect sizes; retire obsolete tasks.
current_claim.audit_question: What part of this task can create failure, which system conditions enable it, and would a simpler or absent intervention be better?
current_claim.change_note: Retains native human-factors boundary and explicitly rejects universal operator-blame extrapolation.

properties.current_name: Age-based preventive maintenance only for valid age-related mechanisms

native_record.PROPERTY_NAME: Age-based preventive maintenance only for valid age-related mechanisms
native_record.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Replacement theory and scheduled overhaul; narrowed by airline RCM evidence and modern life-data modelling.
native_record.ORIGINAL_FORM: Replace or overhaul at a fixed age to avoid wear-out.
native_record.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Scheduled intervention cannot reduce random/weakly age-related failures and may introduce maintenance faults or waste useful life.
native_record.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Reduce mission failure or lifecycle consequence by acting before a demonstrable age-related risk rise.
native_record.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: A convenient age limit is imposed without a dominant wear-out mode, stable age relationship or evidence that overhaul restores resistance.
native_record.MECHANISM: Identify failure mechanism and conditional age-risk; estimate survival/uncertainty; compare maintenance-induced risk and cost; verify post-task reliability.
native_record.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Dominant wear-out, fatigue, corrosion, consumable depletion or legally/physically bounded life with observable age/exposure.
native_record.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Run to failure, inspect condition or use simple replacement-on-failure when consequence and restoration support permit.
native_record.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Mechanism-specific life data, exposure rather than calendar age where appropriate, restoration-effect evidence and maintenance quality.
native_record.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
native_record.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
native_record.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
native_record.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
native_record.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
native_record.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.
native_record.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents predictable wear-out while avoiding ritual overhaul of items without useful age limits.
native_record.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Maintenance planner, asset/fleet owner and mission-risk authority.
native_record.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Calendar age used instead of cycles/stress; mixture populations; changed materials; overhaul not as-good-as-new; invasive task causes failure.
native_record.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The famous RCM pattern proportions are aircraft-specific; they justify mechanism testing, not a universal claim that age never matters.
native_record.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Universal scheduled overhaul narrowed to mechanism- and consequence-specific age tasks with field-data refresh.
native_record.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A maintenance interval justified by a causal degradation mechanism, exposure model, uncertainty, task effectiveness and net-consequence comparison.
native_record.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A preventive-maintenance calendar is not the property; intervention before a validated age-linked risk is.
native_record.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Nowlan and Heap found multiple age-reliability patterns and set applicability conditions for scheduled rework rather than endorsing universal intervals (SRC-008).
native_record.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Strong wear-out mechanisms and finite-life items provide robust contexts where age-based replacement is retained.
native_record.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should sparse field data be pooled across configurations without erasing mechanism differences?

current_claim.bearer: An age-based inspection/replacement policy for an item and failure consequence.
current_claim.proposition: Scheduled age replacement should be justified by its expected consequence under a defensible age/exposure model and task effect, not by a presumed universal wear-out curve.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: Under a memoryless life with perfect instantaneous renewal and positive planned cost, the illustrated age replacement adds cost without reducing the inherent failure intensity. Other hazards, constraints or conservative uncertainty can justify other policies.
current_claim.model_domain: Renewal cost rates are conditional on life law, repair quality, duration and costs. Physical mechanism evidence strengthens transport but no universal optimum follows from a fitted shape.
current_claim.mechanism: Replaces or renews an item before failure when age meaningfully changes exposure; may instead add unnecessary intervention.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Scheduled maintenance, condition inspection, replacement on failure or an explicit bounded precaution.
current_claim.positive_scope: Mechanism-supported wear-out policies and carefully declared uncertainty/constraint-based limits.
current_claim.negative_scope: No universal bathtub, universal RCM age-pattern proportions or universal claim that scheduled maintenance is wasteful.
current_claim.counterexample: C05's exponential policy costs1.2858versus1per time unit; its selected wear-out model costs.6093versus1.1284. Both comparisons assume instantaneous perfect replacement and invented costs.
current_claim.criterion: Specify age/exposure, renewal effect, downtime and induced faults, missed-failure consequence and comparator; test sensitivity to uncertain assumptions.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: NASA's documented later RCM uptake and conditional constructed models; original1978report and its aircraft dataset were not freshly read.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Hazard/age relationship, informative withdrawal, task efficacy, constraints, costs and field correspondence.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: Run to failure, simple inspection or replacement on failure when consequence and support allow.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Include planned labor, downtime, new-part defects and disposal; retire an interval whose protected mechanism or benefit no longer exists.
current_claim.audit_question: What does age change in this item, what does the intervention reset, and what evidence beats a simpler allowed policy?
current_claim.change_note: Preserves the native rejection of routine age folklore while allowing explicit decision under uncertainty rather than demanding complete causal knowledge.

properties.current_name: Condition-based and predictive maintenance only with observable precursors and decision value

native_record.PROPERTY_NAME: Condition-based and predictive maintenance only with observable precursors and decision value
native_record.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: On-condition RCM, machinery condition monitoring, PHM and modern ML/digital-twin predictive maintenance.
native_record.ORIGINAL_FORM: Inspect a condition indicator before the P–F interval expires or predict remaining useful life to schedule work.
native_record.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Fixed schedules waste life, but predictions can be uncalibrated, late, false-positive or non-transferable and can trigger harmful maintenance.
native_record.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Detect actionable degradation with enough lead time and confidence that intervention reduces expected mission/lifecycle loss.
native_record.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: No stable precursor; sensor drift; domain shift; uncertain RUL ignored; maintenance action ineffective; false alarms dominate; lead time shorter than logistics delay.
native_record.MECHANISM: Validate precursor-to-failure relation, sensor chain, uncertainty, lead-time distribution and intervention effect; optimise against simple policies; monitor drift.
native_record.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Failure mechanisms with measurable deterioration, sufficient lead time, meaningful consequence and an effective intervention.
native_record.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Use inspection, fixed replacement or run-to-failure when a simple policy performs similarly or data/precursors are inadequate.
native_record.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Reliable sensing, labelled/field failure data, calibrated uncertainty, domain representativeness, maintenance capacity and action-cost model.
native_record.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
native_record.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
native_record.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
native_record.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Enumerated fault/failure population, observable signals, calibrated thresholds, isolation resolution, false-alarm and missed-detection costs.
native_record.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
native_record.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.
native_record.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Targets intervention where it can avert failure while reducing needless planned maintenance.
native_record.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Maintenance planner, asset owner, operator and logistics manager.
native_record.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Benchmark overfit; synthetic-data gap; leakage; censored labels; black-box confidence; alert fatigue; action changes the data-generating process.
native_record.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The literature is heterogeneous and often laboratory/dataset-centric; no evidence supports universal superiority over simpler policies.
native_record.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Threshold condition monitoring expanded to probabilistic PHM, hybrid physics/data models, uncertainty and decision-aware maintenance.
native_record.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A field-calibrated, uncertainty-aware precursor and intervention case compared against a cheap baseline under the actual loss function.
native_record.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A “predictive maintenance” platform or RUL number is not the property; demonstrated earlier/better decisions are.
native_record.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Systematic reviews show rapid growth but heterogeneous applications; the 2026 PHM review treats uncertainty as unavoidable throughout deployment (SRC-071–SRC-073).
native_record.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Well-instrumented monotonic degradation with proven intervention can yield strong value; the result remains mechanism-specific.
native_record.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How often do published gains survive cross-site transfer and prospective comparison with simple maintenance rules?

FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT: Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.END_EFFECT: No stable precursor; sensor drift; domain shift; uncertain RUL ignored; maintenance action ineffective; false alarms dominate; lead time shorter than logistics delay.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.PROPAGATION_PATH: Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY: A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.DEPENDENCIES: Reliable sensing, labelled/field failure data, calibrated uncertainty, domain representativeness, maintenance capacity and action-cost model.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING: Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.LATENT_CONDITION: Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.DETECTION: Outcome- or function-relevant observation, not a component heartbeat alone.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.MISSED_DETECTION_COST: Continued propagation, latent damage, missed recovery window or false assurance.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.AMBIGUITY_GROUPS: Plausible causes producing the same symptom are preserved until discriminated.
