FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.NEXT_LEVEL_EFFECT: Effect on the enclosing function, dependency path or maintenance process.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.END_EFFECT: Logs share failed control plane; clocks diverge; restart erases state; auto-remediation loops; high volume drops key evidence; recovery contaminates artefacts. Current limitation: No log-everything or independent-telemetry-stack requirement; no inferred competence from data volume.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.PROPAGATION_PATH: Functional, physical, state, timing, control, resource or organisational coupling.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY: A declared fault-containment region or explicit stop/degradation boundary.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.DEPENDENCIES: Measurement correctness, retention access, clock/order meaning, feasible analysis and accepted collection constraints.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.COMMON_CAUSE_OR_SHARED_COUPLING: Shared specification, environment, supplier, control plane, state, maintenance or operator path must be challenged.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.LATENT_CONDITION: Standby, monitoring, repair or dependency defects may remain latent until demand.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.DETECTION: Function-relevant observation at the claimed boundary; a component heartbeat can suffice when it directly observes the complete required binary function. It does not establish a wider end-to-end function merely by being green.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.CONTROL: Retains before/after state, symptoms and actions that recovery may otherwise erase.
FAILURE_PROPAGATION_PROFILE.RESIDUAL_RISK: Unmodeled combinations, dependence, observation gaps and changed conditions remain possible. A valid bounded containment contribution need not establish diagnosis or complete restoration.

REDUNDANCY_COMMON_CAUSE_PROFILE.REASON: The property does not itself claim redundancy benefit; any redundant implementation must invoke ERM-P008/ERM-P009.

DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Observability and evidence preservation during failure and recovery
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.TARGET_FAULTS_FAILURES: Logs share failed control plane; clocks diverge; restart erases state; auto-remediation loops; high volume drops key evidence; recovery contaminates artefacts. Current limitation: No log-everything or independent-telemetry-stack requirement; no inferred competence from data volume.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.OBSERVABLES: Function outputs, timing, state, residuals, dependency signals and user/mission outcomes.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.DETECTION_COVERAGE: Coverage is stated for an enumerated fault/failure population, operating mode and latency window.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.FALSE_ALARM_COST: Unnecessary maintenance, failover, shutdown, operator load or customer disruption.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.MISSED_DETECTION_COST: Continued propagation, latent damage, missed recovery window or false assurance.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.ISOLATION_RESOLUTION: Replaceable unit, functional region, dependency or ambiguity group appropriate to the action.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.AMBIGUITY_GROUPS: Plausible causes producing the same symptom are preserved until discriminated.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.LATENCY: Detection and isolation time are bounded relative to propagation and recovery deadlines.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATION: Uncertainty, thresholds, drift and out-of-distribution conditions are exposed.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.OPERATOR_OR_AUTOMATION_ACTION: Action is authority-bounded, reversible where feasible and matched to diagnosis confidence.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.RECOVERY_COVERAGE: Count a detected event as successfully restored or contained only for the separately declared action outcome and denominator. A true detected event remains detected even when restoration is absent or unresolved. Detection, isolation, containment and restoration coverage are reported separately.
DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Preserving relevant observations can improve later discrimination and correction, including after a recovery that did not diagnose the cause; observation is not itself diagnosis or protected operation. Guard: Collect information that remains available under the target failure and is adequate for a named question. Retention and access must respect actual constraints and cost.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Observability and evidence preservation during failure and recovery
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.INITIATING_FAILURE: Logs share failed control plane; clocks diverge; restart erases state; auto-remediation loops; high volume drops key evidence; recovery contaminates artefacts. Current limitation: No log-everything or independent-telemetry-stack requirement; no inferred competence from data volume.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RECOVERY_ACTION: Retains before/after state, symptoms and actions that recovery may otherwise erase.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.AUTHORITY_SOURCE: State/configuration identity and the actual authority relevant to the action or claim. A pure model has no external action authority; a bounded internal restore does not by itself establish authority to resume a wider service.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.CHECKPOINT_BACKUP_SPARE_OR_ALTERNATE: Declared checkpoint, replica, backup, spare, rebuild source or manual workaround.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RPO_OR_STATE_LOSS_BOUND: State/data loss bound where the function depends on preserved state; explicitly state a nontrigger for stateless or directly reconstructible functions.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND: The declared restoration interval or bound, if the claim requires one. Distinguish detection, waiting, logistics, repair and validation and avoid summing overlapping intervals.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.STATE_RECONCILIATION: Reconcile the state required by the named restored function. Broader divergent or external state may remain an explicit residual; authoritative wider service requires its own relevant conditions.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS: Retain sufficient trustworthy evidence to determine impact, state, likely causes, actions and post-recovery correctness within time/privacy constraints. Current scope: Minimal deterministic evidence and richer instrumentation where materially useful.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS: Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS: Verify dependencies that the particular restoration claim requires. Record unverified external dependencies separately; they prevent an unsupported wider completion claim but do not erase a valid internal postcondition.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.VALIDATION: An observation or proof adequate to the named functional/state postcondition. Independent end-to-end checks are appropriate when the claim needs them, not a universal prerequisite for every local deterministic restoration.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY: Keep proof of the postcondition separate from actual permission to resume consequential service. Name the relevant decision maker or rule when applicable.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK: A justified bounded fallback where it adds protection. It need not resolve every root cause, and not every restoration claim requires a second full recovery mechanism.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Preserving relevant observations can improve later discrimination and correction, including after a recovery that did not diagnose the cause; observation is not itself diagnosis or protected operation. Guard: Collect information that remains available under the target failure and is adequate for a named question. Retention and access must respect actual constraints and cost.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Observability and evidence preservation during failure and recovery
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CLAIM: Preserving relevant observations can improve later discrimination and correction, including after a recovery that did not diagnose the cause; observation is not itself diagnosis or protected operation. Guard: Collect information that remains available under the target failure and is adequate for a named question. Retention and access must respect actual constraints and cost.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR: Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Identify the hardware, software, data, model, environment, dependency and procedure conditions that the particular claim materially depends on. An exhaustive live inventory is not universally required.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE: Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN: Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. Retrospective observations retain their actual design limits.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MODEL: Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.ASSUMPTIONS: Declare the assumptions actually used, such as independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage or representativeness. Their absence from an unrelated deterministic claim is not automatically a defect.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY: Express uncertainty appropriate to the claim. A stochastic estimate needs its model and uncertainty; an exact deterministic result need not invent a probability interval. A qualitative criterion may remain qualitative.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS: Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.COVERAGE: Empirical inference is limited by the observed population and design; a mathematical or exhaustive finite result can cover its explicitly proved domain. Neither automatically supplies external-system correspondence.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Reproduce a failure, distinguish causes, assess a fix or decide that no further investigation is useful.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Record the minimal reproducer, action and result for a deterministic fault.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: A restart restores service but deletes the only symptom trace; conversely, huge logs collected by the failing shared dependency are unavailable during the event.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS: Reassess evidence when a relevant configuration, profile, environment, support or dependency change alters a premise. No arbitrary periodic expiry or full-retest rule follows for unaffected claims.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Preserving relevant observations can improve later discrimination and correction, including after a recovery that did not diagnose the cause; observation is not itself diagnosis or protected operation. Guard: Collect information that remains available under the target failure and is adequate for a named question. Retention and access must respect actual constraints and cost.

HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Historical attribution retained, with current typed genealogy and exact fresh scopes. No original executed-prompt or earliest-priority inference.

FORMAL_OR_PROBABILISTIC_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: A log is evidence of recorded observations under a measurement process, not a complete causal history. Primary designs, historical observations, operator account and qualitative AI guidance; no measured observability effectiveness or privacy assessment.

LIFE_DATA_OR_FIELD_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Selected reported operating/experimental evidence, if listed; no new empirical dataset received or reanalyzed. Empty list means no such fresh direct evidence assigned to this claim.

DEMONSTRATION_TEST_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Author cases are constructed arithmetic/logical witnesses only. No deployed demonstration or physical/operational test was performed.

INCIDENT_OR_FAILURE_CASE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Listed operator incident accounts support reported mechanisms at those events, not prevalence or independently verified countermeasure effects.

OPERATIONAL_PRACTICE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: Listed normative/practitioner/owner sources explain selected mechanisms, intent or currentness at their access scopes; they are not independent causal efficacy studies.

REPLICATION_OR_MULTI_STUDY_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: No independent replication of the author cases or target field effect. Related source versions, chapters and reports are grouped in the source dependence register.

TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: No target-system transfer established. Measurement correctness, retention access, clock/order meaning, feasible analysis and accepted collection constraints.

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.current_scope_judgment: Collect information that remains available under the target failure and is adequate for a named question. Retention and access must respect actual constraints and cost. No log-everything or independent-telemetry-stack requirement; no inferred competence from data volume.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH.current_scope_judgment: A restart restores service but deletes the only symptom trace; conversely, huge logs collected by the failing shared dependency are unavailable during the event. Primary designs, historical observations, operator account and qualitative AI guidance; no measured observability effectiveness or privacy assessment.

native_audit_unique.POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY: Diagnostic evidence and transparency versus privacy, legal constraints and rapid restoration.
native_audit_unique.QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT:
- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate observability and evidence preservation during failure and recovery?
- Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version?
- Which enumerated failures can the diagnostic detect and isolate within the required latency, and what are the false-positive and false-negative costs?
- Does recovery close on independently checked required function, state and dependency postconditions rather than process restart or procedure completion?
- What population, denominator, model, confidence, censoring rule and expiry condition bound the reliability claim?

current_audit_questions: Which later decision needs this evidence, can the target failure erase it, and does retaining more data actually improve discrimination?
Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?
What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

properties.current_name: Proportional cheap path and deterministic functional check

native_record.PROPERTY_NAME: Proportional cheap path and deterministic functional check
native_record.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Tailoring in military/NASA R&M, objectives-based dependability management and decision-focused testing.
native_record.ORIGINAL_FORM: Tailor the reliability programme to mission class and risk.
native_record.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Full FMEA, probabilistic model, demonstration, SLO or chaos programme can cost more than the uncertainty it resolves and become ceremony.
native_record.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Obtain enough trustworthy evidence for the actual decision at proportionate cost and risk.
native_record.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Mandatory artefact regardless of consequence; model precision without decision sensitivity; repeated test after result cannot change action; analysis delays simple fix.
native_record.MECHANISM: State decision/uncertainty/consequence; ask whether a direct functional check, conservative bound, simple design change or acceptance is sufficient; escalate only when needed.
native_record.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Every proposed reliability activity; especially low-consequence, reversible, small-scope or already-observable work.
native_record.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: This property is the cheap path: simplest evidence/mechanism that resolves the live decision while preserving critical assumptions.
native_record.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Clear decision consumer, consequence, reversibility, uncertainty and authority to tailor.
native_record.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
native_record.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
native_record.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
native_record.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
native_record.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
native_record.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
native_record.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Preserves engineering attention for material failure risks and resists reliability bureaucracy.
native_record.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Decision owner, mission/service owner and engineering team.
native_record.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Under-analysis disguised as agility; consequence underestimated; direct check misses latent/tail risk; tailoring used to avoid inconvenient evidence.
native_record.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Proportionality is judgement-sensitive and can rationalise weak assurance; explicit rationale and triggers for escalation are needed.
native_record.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Prescriptive activity lists increasingly coexist with objectives-based, tailored, decision-relevant R&M practice.
native_record.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A documented minimum-sufficient path with escalation criteria, not a blanket waiver or blanket process.
native_record.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: No named artefact is privileged; only the evidence/mechanism needed for the decision survives.
native_record.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Incident reports support targeted safeguards and tests tied to actual mechanisms rather than indiscriminate activity expansion (SRC-058–SRC-061).
native_record.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: High-consequence irreversible missions often justify expensive evidence even when probability is low.
native_record.OPEN_QUESTIONS: Can value-of-information thresholds be operationalised without turning proportionality itself into a new ceremony?

current_claim.bearer: An evidence/control choice for a specified engineering decision.
current_claim.proposition: The simplest adequate check or mechanism is a valid reliability practice when it addresses the live uncertainty and preserves applicable obligations.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: Adequacy is relative to the asserted property and consequence. Cheapness cannot excuse a known unmet requirement or relabel a weak test as a stronger probabilistic guarantee.
current_claim.model_domain: A deterministic check proves its predicate under its execution conditions; broader reliability needs broader evidence.
current_claim.mechanism: Avoids control and evidence burden that adds no useful discrimination, freeing attention for actual risks.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Choose a direct test, focused analysis, bounded manual action or escalation.
current_claim.positive_scope: Low-consequence reversible tasks and narrowly defined deterministic claims; proportionate expensive work where needed.
current_claim.negative_scope: No blanket waiver, universal minimalism or imposed paperwork to justify a trivial check.
current_claim.counterexample: C14'sordered-and-same-sum check is cheap but fails the full permutation requirement; it is adequate only if the weaker predicate is actually the requirement or its residual risk is accepted.
current_claim.criterion: Ask whether the selected check distinguishes the materially different worlds that would change the decision.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Historical/practitioner tailoring and an analytical discriminator; no universal cost-optimal algorithm.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Actual requirement, consequence, authority and completeness of the considered discriminator.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: This is the cheap path: use existing valid evidence or a direct functional check before inventing a standing programme.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Additional checks can create delay and maintenance; remove duplicates that cannot change warranted understanding or action.
current_claim.audit_question: What live uncertainty remains, and what is the least burdensome adequate discriminator without overstating its result?
current_claim.change_note: Native proportionality survives and is supported by primary historical tailoring rather than a new universal maturity ladder.

MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE.ENVIRONMENT: Declared physical, software, organisational and dependency environment.
MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE.FAILURE_DEFINITION: Mandatory artefact regardless of consequence; model precision without decision sensitivity; repeated test after result cannot change action; analysis delays simple fix. Current limitation: No blanket waiver, universal minimalism or imposed paperwork to justify a trivial check.
MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE.DEGRADED_ACCEPTABLE_STATE: Only states explicitly accepted by mission/consumer criteria; otherwise none.
MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE.MISSION_TIME_OR_DEMAND: Specified interval, number of demands or service-measurement window.
MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE.CONSUMER: Choose a direct test, focused analysis, bounded manual action or escalation.
MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: This is the cheap path: use existing valid evidence or a direct functional check before inventing a standing programme.
MISSION_RELIABILITY_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: The simplest adequate check or mechanism is a valid reliability practice when it addresses the live uncertainty and preserves applicable obligations. Guard: Adequacy is relative to the asserted property and consequence. Cheapness cannot excuse a known unmet requirement or relabel a weak test as a stronger probabilistic guarantee.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Proportional cheap path and deterministic functional check
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CLAIM: The simplest adequate check or mechanism is a valid reliability practice when it addresses the live uncertainty and preserves applicable obligations. Guard: Adequacy is relative to the asserted property and consequence. Cheapness cannot excuse a known unmet requirement or relabel a weak test as a stronger probabilistic guarantee.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR: Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Identify the hardware, software, data, model, environment, dependency and procedure conditions that the particular claim materially depends on. An exhaustive live inventory is not universally required.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE: Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN: Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. Retrospective observations retain their actual design limits.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MODEL: Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.ASSUMPTIONS: Declare the assumptions actually used, such as independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage or representativeness. Their absence from an unrelated deterministic claim is not automatically a defect.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY: Express uncertainty appropriate to the claim. A stochastic estimate needs its model and uncertainty; an exact deterministic result need not invent a probability interval. A qualitative criterion may remain qualitative.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS: Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.COVERAGE: Empirical inference is limited by the observed population and design; a mathematical or exhaustive finite result can cover its explicitly proved domain. Neither automatically supplies external-system correspondence.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Choose a direct test, focused analysis, bounded manual action or escalation.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: This is the cheap path: use existing valid evidence or a direct functional check before inventing a standing programme.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: C14'sordered-and-same-sum check is cheap but fails the full permutation requirement; it is adequate only if the weaker predicate is actually the requirement or its residual risk is accepted.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS: Reassess evidence when a relevant configuration, profile, environment, support or dependency change alters a premise. No arbitrary periodic expiry or full-retest rule follows for unaffected claims.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: The simplest adequate check or mechanism is a valid reliability practice when it addresses the live uncertainty and preserves applicable obligations. Guard: Adequacy is relative to the asserted property and consequence. Cheapness cannot excuse a known unmet requirement or relabel a weak test as a stronger probabilistic guarantee.

native_audit_unique.POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY: Proportional assurance cost versus the risk of under-analysing apparently simple work.
native_audit_unique.QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT:
- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate proportional cheap path and deterministic functional check?
- Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version?
- What population, denominator, model, confidence, censoring rule and expiry condition bound the reliability claim?
- Could a cheaper deterministic end-to-end functional check establish the needed state with less modelling and operational risk?

current_audit_questions: What live uncertainty remains, and what is the least burdensome adequate discriminator without overstating its result?
Which of the stated guard and remaining premises are established for the actual function, and which remain unknown?
What cheaper or simpler alternative is adequate at this consequence, and what evidence would justify retaining or retiring this mechanism?

native_record.PROPERTY_NAME: Retirement of stale controls, metrics, support and reliability claims
native_record.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Configuration/obsolescence management, field-data refresh and metric-governance practice.
native_record.ORIGINAL_FORM: Review reliability predictions, maintenance plans and support resources periodically.
native_record.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Controls, thresholds, spares, procedures, models and dashboards persist after configuration/profile/consumer change and create false assurance or burden.
native_record.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Only current, decision-relevant reliability controls and support capabilities govern the current system.
native_record.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Obsolete spare/tool; unsupported dependency; stale profile; dead alert; inherited “nine”; old backup format; handbook rate for changed technology.
native_record.MECHANISM: Attach owner, scope, evidence, configuration, review/expiry and retirement trigger; monitor obsolescence; remove or replace controls that no longer discriminate risk.
native_record.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Technology/configuration/profile/consumer change, repeated false alarms, unused metric, support deprecation or expired evidence.
native_record.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Delete a stale metric/control when no consumer or decision can be named; retain a simple direct check if still useful.
native_record.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Inventory and ownership, configuration/dependency change signals, evidence lineage and authority to retire contractual/process residue.
native_record.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
native_record.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
native_record.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
native_record.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
native_record.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
native_record.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.
native_record.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces false confidence, alert/maintenance burden and unsupported recovery dependence.
native_record.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: System/service owner, maintainer, operator, procurement and assurance authority.
native_record.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Zombie dashboard; contract inertia; metric tied to bonus; unsupported library/part; retirement removes latent protection; no replacement evidence.
native_record.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Frequent change can erode comparability and institutional memory; retirement needs archival trace and consequence check.
native_record.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Periodic document review broadened to live evidence freshness, control efficacy, dependency support and obsolescence risk.
native_record.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Every material reliability control has a current consumer, evidence basis, configuration scope, expiry and safe retirement/replacement path.
native_record.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Keeping a metric because it exists is ceremony; deliberate retention or retirement is the property.
native_record.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: The MIL-HDBK-217 critique shows how outdated data/models can persist institutionally after technology changes (SRC-047).
native_record.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Long-lived controls may encode rare lessons; deletion without historical analysis can reintroduce old failure modes.
native_record.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What evidence should trigger retirement when the protected failure is rare and absence may reflect the control’s success?

current_claim.bearer: A reliability control, metric, support duty or claim over its lifecycle.
current_claim.proposition: A stale or duplicate control/claim can be retired when its protected obligation is absent or adequately covered elsewhere; retirement is itself a decision about retained protection and transition cost.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: No named current consumer is a reason to investigate, not automatic proof that a latent safety/contractual obligation vanished. Establish the applicable boundary before deletion.
current_claim.model_domain: Documentation age and usage are observations; adequacy of remaining protection is a substantive engineering judgment.
current_claim.mechanism: Removes unnecessary burden and misleading assurance while retaining historical comparability where useful.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Remove, replace, simplify, archive or keep with a stated rationale.
current_claim.positive_scope: Obsolete metrics, redundant exercises, unsupported claims and genuinely unused support duties.
current_claim.negative_scope: No arbitrary expiry timer, novelty target or automatic deletion because a control did not recently fire.
current_claim.counterexample: A dormant protective test has no recent incident but still covers a high-consequence demand; a retired metric without archived definitions breaks trend interpretation.
current_claim.criterion: Name what it protects, what remains after removal, transition/rollback needs and which evidence would reverse the decision.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Tailoring/lifecycle guidance and analytical comparison; no current target control was removed or adopted.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Actual obligations, coverage overlap, consumer needs, history and change effects.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: Archive a stale claim, reduce frequency or keep one direct check rather than replacing it with another programme.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Include migration, archival trace, retraining and possible loss of institutional knowledge as well as saved effort.
current_claim.audit_question: What protection or obligation would disappear if this were removed, and is the remaining arrangement demonstrably adequate for the stated scope?
current_claim.change_note: Qualifies native 'delete when no consumer can be named' so absence of a named consumer is not treated as proof of absent obligation.

properties.current_name: Design diversity as conditional common-mode mitigation

native_record.PROPERTY_NAME: Design diversity as conditional common-mode mitigation
native_record.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: N-version programming, diverse hardware/software channels and common-cause mitigation.
native_record.ORIGINAL_FORM: Develop multiple independent versions and vote to tolerate design faults.
native_record.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Identical redundancy shares systematic faults; diversity may reduce common modes but independence is not guaranteed.
native_record.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: At least one/adjudicated implementation remains correct for the target input/fault class without shared specification/model/tool failure.
native_record.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Common specification ambiguity; difficult inputs induce similar errors; shared algorithm/library/data/model; voter/acceptance test wrong; diversity overwhelms maintenance.
native_record.MECHANISM: Diversify selected causal dimensions; analyse shared assumptions; use independent evidence/teams/tools where valuable; test coincident errors; preserve diagnosability and update compatibility.
native_record.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Systematic design/software/model failure dominates and consequence justifies multiple implementations.
native_record.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Prefer one simple implementation plus strong specification/tests when diversity cost and shared assumptions erase benefit.
native_record.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Clear specification/oracle, adjudication, independent causal pathways, configuration control, joint-failure evidence and maintenance capacity.
native_record.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
native_record.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
native_record.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: Credible failure-domain independence, common-cause analysis, standby condition, switchover coverage and state compatibility.
native_record.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
native_record.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
native_record.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
native_record.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Can reduce some common design faults that identical replicas cannot tolerate.
native_record.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Architect, mission authority, software/reliability owner and maintainer.
native_record.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Correlated mistakes; shared training data/model; specification error; voter failure; patch divergence; extra interfaces and operational burden.
native_record.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Knight–Leveson and Eckhardt–Lee directly undermine naïve independence; “different code” is not “independent failure.”
native_record.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: N-version slogans narrowed toward targeted causal diversity with explicit common assumptions, joint testing and lifecycle cost.
native_record.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A quantified/argued diversity case naming which common modes are reduced, which remain shared, adjudication coverage and maintenance/recovery consequences.
native_record.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Separate teams or languages are not the property; reduced joint failure for identified causes is.
native_record.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Homogeneous ecosystem updates can propagate broadly (SRC-061, SRC-062), but empirical multiversion studies show diversity cannot be assumed independent (SRC-014).
native_record.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Properly chosen physical, technological or supplier diversity can materially reduce specific common causes.
native_record.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can diversity benefit be measured for modern AI/model/data stacks where many hidden assumptions are shared?

native_record.DISPOSITION_RATIONALE: Admitted or rejected according to mechanism, trigger, assumption validity, evidence and anti-ceremony analysis.

current_claim.bearer: Diverse implementations/channels and their adjudication or fallback mechanism.
current_claim.proposition: Design diversity can reduce selected shared design failures, but different code or teams do not establish independent failure; benefit depends on distinct rescue behavior and the added adjudication/maintenance paths.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: Specify which common modes are reduced and which requirements, tools, inputs or decision logic remain shared. Evaluate each diversity claim within its population and fault model.
current_claim.model_domain: Joint-event mathematics permits benefit under dependence; empirical independence is not guaranteed by organizational separation.
current_claim.mechanism: Creates an alternative that can respond correctly in cases where the primary fails, with comparison/acceptance/transfer logic.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Use a diverse alternate, strengthen one implementation, improve specifications or accept the residual.
current_claim.positive_scope: Diversity with bounded evidence, including correlated channels with positive rescue probability.
current_claim.negative_scope: Neither a correlated-failure experiment nor one successful pair proves all diversity harmful or all diversity effective.
current_claim.counterexample: Knight–Leveson's27versions of one application failed dependently under its tested inputs; C02shows why dependence can reduce a product-formula prediction without forcing zero benefit.
current_claim.criterion: Inspect the shared specification, input distribution, oracle, rescue set, voter/acceptance failures and ongoing configuration burden.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Main primary multiversion study at its actual scope plus primary design arguments; no independent replication or universal effect size.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Different failure manifestations, representative demands, correct adjudication, capacity and maintenance quality.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: One simpler implementation with a sound specification and direct tests may be better than diverse complexity.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Diverse tools/skills, duplicated updates, state differences and diagnosis can outweigh rescue value; retire alternatives whose protection is not worth retaining.
current_claim.audit_question: Which failure cases does diversity actually rescue, what remains common, and could adjudication or maintenance erase the benefit?
current_claim.change_note: Preserves native conditional diversity and prevents the historical contrary experiment from becoming a universal rejection.

native_audit_unique.POSSIBLE_CONFLICTING_PROPERTY: Design diversity versus maintainability, verification cost and shared-specification error.
native_audit_unique.QUESTIONS_FOR_REPOSITORY_AUDIT:
- Does the target define the required function, failure threshold, consumer and operating conditions needed to evaluate design diversity as conditional common-mode mitigation?
- Is the evidence for this property bound to the current configuration and a representative operational profile rather than inherited from a label, template or prior version?
- Are the supposed redundant channels actually separate failure domains, and is detection, switchover, state transfer and degraded capacity covered?

properties.current_name: MTBF as a universal scalar for reliability

native_record.PROPERTY_NAME: MTBF as a universal scalar for reliability
native_record.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Constant-rate electronic reliability prediction and repairable-system HPP practice.
native_record.ORIGINAL_FORM: Represent reliability by mean time between failures, often as the reciprocal of a constant failure rate.
native_record.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A convenient scalar is used to compare items and plan tests/spares.
native_record.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: No standalone required function is protected; MTBF is an estimand only under a defined recurrent-event process and failure definition.
native_record.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Mean hides mission time, hazard shape, tail, repair, severity, dependence and functional consequence; constant-rate premise is unstated.
native_record.MECHANISM: Rejected as a universal property; retain MTBF only as a model-qualified descriptive measure with confidence and exposure.
native_record.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Only when recurrent failures are reasonably represented by HPP/constant intensity or as an explicitly limited empirical mean.
native_record.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Report exposure, failure count/intensity, uncertainty and mission reliability directly.
native_record.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stable failure definition, repairable-system process, representative exposure, constant-intensity validation if exponential inference is made.
native_record.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
native_record.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
native_record.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
native_record.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
native_record.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
native_record.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
native_record.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Limited: compact planning/comparison measure inside its valid model.
native_record.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Test planner, maintenance/logistics analyst or model user—not a generic mission consumer.
native_record.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: “MTBF 100,000 h” read as life; reciprocal used without constant hazard; mixed failures; no confidence; predicted part rates summed as field truth.
native_record.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: NIST makes the constant-rate assumption explicit; the National Academies critique documents handbook misuse and inaccurate predictions.
native_record.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Universal slogan narrowed to one estimand among mission reliability, failure intensity, life distribution and availability measures.
native_record.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use only with declared model, failure population, exposure, confidence and decision; never substitute it for mission or field reliability.
native_record.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The target/slogan is ceremony when detached from model and mission.
native_record.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Field and incident data show severity and correlated outages can dominate a mean interval.
native_record.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: MTBF remains mathematically coherent and operationally useful in some stationary repairable-system contexts.
native_record.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What communication formats most reliably prevent non-experts from reading MTBF as expected lifetime?

current_claim.bearer: An MTBF/MTTF estimate and the stronger reliability claim someone attaches to it.
current_claim.proposition: A mean can be a valid descriptive or model quantity but cannot serve as a universal scalar for mission reliability, outage consequences or all lifetime behavior.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: A finite mean does not require an exponential distribution. Constant hazard/HPP assumptions are needed for particular formulas and inferences, not for the existence of every MTBF-like mean. State whether downtime is included.
current_claim.model_domain: Definitions and expectations are mathematical; a measured mean requires a valid sample/observation process.
current_claim.mechanism: Rejects the invalid inference from one mean to a full distribution, consumer consequence or applicable future population.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Retain a useful scoped mean, add a tail/mission measure or abandon an irrelevant scalar.
current_claim.positive_scope: Correctly defined means with units, exposure, uncertainty and purpose.
current_claim.negative_scope: Universal 'MTBF equals reliability' inference remains rejected; the rejection does not ban mean measures.
current_claim.counterexample: Equal average downtime can hide different outage patterns; a mean lifetime alone does not imply a memoryless residual life.
current_claim.criterion: Name the random quantity, population, time basis, uncertainty and which receiving question the mean answers.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Primary statistical guidance and review plus analytic distinctions; no empirical field MTBF is estimated.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Finite mean, representativeness, censoring, model fit and external correspondence.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: Report count/exposure and an appropriate interval, mission event or relevant outage duration.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Remove a prestige scalar when it obscures decisions; retain valid history/definitions if useful for comparison.
current_claim.audit_question: Is this mean being used outside its definition or sampling model, and what important behavior remains unidentified?
current_claim.change_note: Preserves original ceremony rejection but corrects any reading that all mean time measures require constant hazard.

native_record.PROPERTY_NAME: “Five nines” as a universal service-reliability claim
native_record.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Telecommunications/high-availability uptime targets and later service marketing/SRE shorthand.
native_record.ORIGINAL_FORM: Express annual allowed downtime by counting nines of availability.
native_record.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Communicate a compact availability objective.
native_record.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: No universal function; validity requires a specific SLI, denominator, scope, consumer, window and exclusions.
native_record.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Nines hide whether failures are one long outage or many interruptions, which users/regions/journeys count, degraded service, data correctness and correlated dependency loss.
native_record.MECHANISM: Reject the slogan as evidence; translate to consumer journeys, outage distribution, tails, consequence and recovery objectives.
native_record.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Only as shorthand after full metric semantics are already defined and understood.
native_record.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: State maximum tolerable outage patterns or direct user/mission outcomes instead.
native_record.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Valid SLI/denominator, complete telemetry, user weighting, interval, planned-maintenance treatment and outage-shape analysis.
native_record.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
native_record.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
native_record.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
native_record.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
native_record.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
native_record.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.

properties.current_name: Universal bathtub-curve assumption

native_record.PROPERTY_NAME: Universal bathtub-curve assumption
native_record.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Early lifetime/hazard modelling and an influential three-phase graphical idealisation.
native_record.ORIGINAL_FORM: Assume every product has infant mortality, a constant-hazard useful life, then wear-out.
native_record.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Provide an intuitive lifecycle story for screening, random failures and replacement.
native_record.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: No standalone mission property; it is a candidate hazard-shape model.
native_record.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Observed modes/populations do not exhibit all phases; mixtures create aggregate shape; item changes/maintenance violate stationary phases; policy follows the sketch rather than data/mechanism.
native_record.MECHANISM: Reject universality; fit/compare distributions and mechanisms, stratify populations, use repairable-event models where appropriate.
native_record.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Use only when mechanism and data support the relevant segment for the decision.
native_record.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Plot empirical hazard/ROCOF with uncertainty or use a conservative nonparametric bound.
native_record.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Life data with censoring, homogeneous enough population, mechanism knowledge, exposure and model diagnostics.
native_record.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
native_record.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
native_record.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
native_record.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
native_record.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
native_record.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: Access, modularity, safe isolation, procedures, test equipment, spares, tools, skills, logistics, configuration data and time under actual field conditions.
native_record.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Limited conceptual aid when its phases actually match the system.
native_record.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Reliability analyst and maintenance planner.
native_record.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Forced constant hazard; age replacement without wear-out; burn-in for non-infant modes; population mixture; repairable system treated as lifetime sample.
native_record.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Peer-reviewed critique and RCM field evidence directly reject universal use.
native_record.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: A universal lifecycle picture narrowed to one possible hazard pattern among many, with mechanism-specific maintenance.
native_record.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Treat the bathtub as a hypothesis/teaching model, never an assumed empirical law.
native_record.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The curve on a slide is ceremony when it predetermines policy.
native_record.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Nowlan and Heap’s aircraft component study documented six patterns and set mechanism-specific maintenance conditions (SRC-008).
native_record.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Some physical products genuinely show early defects, a useful-life plateau and wear-out; local use remains valid.
native_record.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How often are aggregate bathtub shapes artefacts of heterogeneous cohorts rather than individual mechanisms?

current_claim.bearer: An assumed population hazard shape.
current_claim.proposition: A bathtub-shaped hazard is a possible model, not a universal empirical law of components, repairable systems or software.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: Use a hazard shape only within its population/mechanism and observation assumptions. A shape may be useful for teaching or conditional reasoning without proving field fit.
current_claim.model_domain: Weibull shapes, mixtures and constant hazards provide explicit alternatives; repairable event intensity is not automatically first-life hazard.
current_claim.mechanism: Prevents unsupported age policies and predictions from a familiar schematic.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Select or compare a life model, collect relevant exposure, use bounds or decline an age claim.
current_claim.positive_scope: A supported bathtub pattern in a defined population and a labelled illustrative model.

native_record.PROPERTY_NAME: Handbook reliability prediction as field-reliability proof
native_record.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: RCA and MIL-HDBK-217 component-rate prediction programmes.
native_record.ORIGINAL_FORM: Sum adjusted generic component failure rates to predict equipment MTBF before fielding.
native_record.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Support design comparison, requirements allocation and early planning before sufficient field data exist.
native_record.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: No direct field function is established by the table; it is a model output for a declared design/environment.
native_record.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Outdated database, constant-rate form, missing mechanisms, wrong use conditions, deterministic point output and contractual ritual are presented as achieved reliability.
native_record.MECHANISM: Reject equivalence; use physics/mechanism and field calibration, uncertainty, sensitivity and comparative purpose only where validated.
native_record.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Early comparative design or planning when no better evidence exists and limitations are explicit.
native_record.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Use qualitative stress/margin review, targeted tests and field analogues when a numerical point prediction adds false precision.
native_record.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Technology/current data, environmental/profile match, mechanism relevance, uncertainty and calibration.
native_record.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
native_record.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
native_record.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
native_record.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
native_record.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
native_record.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
native_record.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: At most, rough comparison or allocation under controlled assumptions.
native_record.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Design/trade-study and planning authority—not final field acceptance.
native_record.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Obsolete parts data; generic quality factors; no failure mechanisms; multiplicative factors; point prediction; inherited contractual target.
native_record.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: The National Academies appendix reports gross over- and underprediction and concludes the method can mislead.
native_record.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Generic handbook prediction narrowed/replaced by objectives-driven design, physics of failure, empirical field updating and uncertainty.
native_record.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Prediction is labelled model-based, comparative and uncertain; field/mission reliability requires representative evidence.
native_record.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A handbook calculation is ceremony when performed to satisfy a deliverable rather than inform a decision.
native_record.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Technology and use-condition changes documented by the National Academies undermine direct transfer of old generic rates (SRC-047).
native_record.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Some calibrated prediction tools can rank design alternatives; the rejected claim is equality with field truth.
native_record.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What validation criteria are sufficient before a modern prediction model can support absolute rather than comparative claims?

native_record.PROPERTY_NAME: Completed FMEA/FMECA as proof that failure modes are controlled
native_record.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Institutionalised FMEA/FMECA deliverables in military, aerospace, automotive and other programmes.
native_record.ORIGINAL_FORM: Complete and approve a worksheet listing failure modes, effects, criticality and controls.
native_record.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Create systematic visibility and prioritisation of plausible failure modes.
native_record.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: No mission protection follows from completion alone; each important mode needs effective prevention/detection/containment/recovery or accepted residual risk.
native_record.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Copied modes; subjective ranks; missing interactions/software/human factors; “control” untested; document stale; rows closed by wording.
native_record.MECHANISM: Reject completion claim; retain ERM-P006 systematic challenge and bind material rows to design/test/field closure.
native_record.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Use a structured FMEA when bottom-up functional/component analysis is decision-relevant and proportionate.
native_record.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Focused failure challenge or fault tree for the live top event when a full table adds no value.
native_record.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Current design, competent participants, scope/ground rules, interface/dependence analysis and closure evidence.
native_record.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
native_record.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
native_record.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
native_record.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
native_record.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: No recovery premise is inherent; any claim that depends on restoration must invoke explicit recovery postconditions.
native_record.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
native_record.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: The method can find modes; completion itself has no independent payoff.
native_record.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Design, reliability, maintenance and acceptance teams.
native_record.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Checkbox culture; RPN arithmetic; row inflation; stale revision; controls without coverage; multiple-failure blindness.
native_record.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Method limitations and bureaucracy are well documented; modern standards support tailoring rather than universal sufficiency.
native_record.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Worksheet completion narrowed to objective-driven, cross-method, evidence-linked failure analysis.
native_record.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Only claim that defined failure modes were systematically challenged and specific controls verified; never “FMEA complete, therefore reliable.”
native_record.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The approved worksheet is the ceremony; ERM-P006 is the property.
native_record.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: Complex outages involve interacting change, dependency, state and recovery mechanisms that part-by-part completion can omit.
native_record.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Well-executed FMEA remains useful and widely retained; only sufficiency-by-completion is rejected.
native_record.OPEN_QUESTIONS: Which observable indicators distinguish a live, decision-effective FMEA from a compliant but inert one?

properties.current_name: Backup existence as proof that recovery is solved

native_record.PROPERTY_NAME: Backup existence as proof that recovery is solved
native_record.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Backup and contingency-plan compliance.
native_record.ORIGINAL_FORM: Verify that backup jobs run and copies exist.
native_record.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Preserve data/artefacts for loss scenarios.
native_record.REQUIRED_FUNCTION_OR_MISSION: Restored, authoritative and functionally usable state within RPO/RTO—not copy existence.
native_record.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Stale/corrupt/inaccessible/incompatible backup; missing key/tool; incomplete application state; same disaster affects source; restore never tested.
native_record.MECHANISM: Reject existence claim; apply ERM-P017 recurring restore/reconstitution validation.
native_record.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Never sufficient alone; backup is one precondition in a recovery case.
native_record.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For reproducible stateless assets, verify build-from-source and one end-to-end check.
native_record.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Integrity, freshness, isolation, tooling, configuration, capacity, procedures, state semantics and trained staff.
native_record.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_PRECONDITIONS: A declared and sufficiently representative operating profile, environment, duty cycle, mission phase and maintenance state.
native_record.FAILURE_MODEL_PRECONDITIONS: A failure model appropriate to the estimand; distinguish non-repairable life, recurrent repairable events, demand failures, software activation and service outcomes.
native_record.REDUNDANCY_OR_COMMON_CAUSE_PRECONDITIONS: No redundancy premise is needed; if redundancy appears in the implementation, common-cause and switchover assumptions must be analysed separately.
native_record.DIAGNOSTIC_COVERAGE_PRECONDITIONS: Observable functional outcomes sufficient to determine whether the claimed property actually holds.
native_record.RECOVERY_OR_REPAIR_PRECONDITIONS: A valid recovery source, authorised action, state/data reconciliation, dependency readiness and independently checked return-to-service postconditions.
native_record.MAINTAINABILITY_PRECONDITIONS: The design and support system must not make verification or corrective action infeasible.
native_record.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Copy existence has potential value only when the complete recovery path is valid.
native_record.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Data/service owner and continuity authority.
native_record.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Green job; empty archive; partial DB; wrong version; inaccessible credentials; unbounded restore time.
native_record.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Incident evidence directly refutes the equivalence.
native_record.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Backup compliance evolved toward restore exercises, functional validation and reconstitution.
native_record.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use ERM-P017; do not claim recoverability from inventory alone.
native_record.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Backup-count dashboard is the ceremony.
native_record.EMPIRICAL_OR_FIELD_EVIDENCE: GitLab had backup mechanisms that were not working and could not fully recover production data (SRC-060).
native_record.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: A valid backup is necessary in many recovery strategies, just never sufficient.
native_record.OPEN_QUESTIONS: None affecting disposition; optimal exercise frequency remains context-specific.

current_claim.bearer: A stored backup inventory and a recovery capability claim.
current_claim.proposition: Backup existence does not entail that required data or function can be recovered under the relevant loss scenario.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: The invalid implication is rejected. A backup can be valuable evidence of stored state, and a bounded restore demonstration can establish more without proving every disaster.
current_claim.model_domain: Existence of bytes and restored-function predicates are logically different.
current_claim.mechanism: Keeps accessibility, trust, compatibility, dependencies and receiving checks visible.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Test or otherwise substantiate a path, use rebuild, repair the missing resource or accept loss.
current_claim.positive_scope: Validated backup/rebuild at declared scope underC017.
current_claim.negative_scope: Inventory-only recovery assurance rejected; no dismissal of untested bytes as necessarily worthless.
current_claim.counterexample: C04'sinternalrestorationcanholdwhilecredentialandexternalconditionsfail; an encrypted backup without its lost key does not satisfy even the internal restore requirement.
current_claim.criterion: Follow the chain from available source to required state/function and mark each unobserved premise.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Primary mechanisms and logical counterexample; native GitLab2017original is not freshly read in this study.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Recoverable source, permissions, compatible environment, resources, receiving condition and data-loss tolerance.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: Rebuild reproducible stateless assets and perform a direct function check.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Retire redundant backups only after checking remaining loss coverage and applicable retention constraints.
current_claim.audit_question: What evidence beyond possession of bytes establishes the restoration path and its declared result?
current_claim.change_note: Original rejected inference retained with a bounded usable alternative.

Current limitation: Inventory-only recovery assurance rejected; no dismissal of untested bytes as necessarily worthless.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RECOVERY_ACTION: Keeps accessibility, trust, compatibility, dependencies and receiving checks visible.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.AUTHORITY_SOURCE: State/configuration identity and the actual authority relevant to the action or claim. A pure model has no external action authority; a bounded internal restore does not by itself establish authority to resume a wider service.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.CHECKPOINT_BACKUP_SPARE_OR_ALTERNATE: Declared checkpoint, replica, backup, spare, rebuild source or manual workaround.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RPO_OR_STATE_LOSS_BOUND: State/data loss bound where the function depends on preserved state; explicitly state a nontrigger for stateless or directly reconstructible functions.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND: The declared restoration interval or bound, if the claim requires one. Distinguish detection, waiting, logistics, repair and validation and avoid summing overlapping intervals.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.STATE_RECONCILIATION: Reconcile the state required by the named restored function. Broader divergent or external state may remain an explicit residual; authoritative wider service requires its own relevant conditions.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.FUNCTIONAL_POSTCONDITIONS: Restored, authoritative and functionally usable state within RPO/RTO—not copy existence. Current scope: Validated backup/rebuild at declared scope underC017.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.DATA_STATE_POSTCONDITIONS: Integrity, completeness, freshness, ordering and authority appropriate to the mission.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS: Verify dependencies that the particular restoration claim requires. Record unverified external dependencies separately; they prevent an unsupported wider completion claim but do not erase a valid internal postcondition.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.VALIDATION: An observation or proof adequate to the named functional/state postcondition. Independent end-to-end checks are appropriate when the claim needs them, not a universal prerequisite for every local deterministic restoration.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY: Keep proof of the postcondition separate from actual permission to resume consequential service. Name the relevant decision maker or rule when applicable.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK: A justified bounded fallback where it adds protection. It need not resolve every root cause, and not every restoration claim requires a second full recovery mechanism.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Backup existence does not entail that required data or function can be recovered under the relevant loss scenario. Guard: The invalid implication is rejected. A backup can be valuable evidence of stored state, and a bounded restore demonstration can establish more without proving every disaster.

RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.PROPERTY: Backup existence as proof that recovery is solved
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CLAIM: Backup existence does not entail that required data or function can be recovered under the relevant loss scenario. Guard: The invalid implication is rejected. A backup can be valuable evidence of stored state, and a bounded restore demonstration can establish more without proving every disaster.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.POPULATION_OR_DENOMINATOR: Declared units, missions, demands, requests, users, time windows or recurrent-event process.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Identify the hardware, software, data, model, environment, dependency and procedure conditions that the particular claim materially depends on. An exhaustive live inventory is not universally required.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.OPERATIONAL_PROFILE: Representative demand/workload/environment with consequence-important rare cases identified.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.TEST_OR_OBSERVATION_DESIGN: Use a design adequate to the estimand: sampling, censoring, exposure and stopping assumptions for stochastic inference; an exact predicate and finite domain for a deterministic check. Retrospective observations retain their actual design limits.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MODEL: Model selected for the stated estimand: life distribution, recurrent-event process, binomial demand, availability state model or direct functional check.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.ASSUMPTIONS: Declare the assumptions actually used, such as independence, stationarity, censoring, repair effectiveness, acceleration, coverage or representativeness. Their absence from an unrelated deterministic claim is not automatically a defect.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONFIDENCE_OR_UNCERTAINTY: Express uncertainty appropriate to the claim. A stochastic estimate needs its model and uncertainty; an exact deterministic result need not invent a probability interval. A qualitative criterion may remain qualitative.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CENSORING_AND_MISSINGNESS: Right/interval censoring, unreported events, lost telemetry and excluded windows are recorded.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.COVERAGE: Empirical inference is limited by the observed population and design; a mathematical or exhaustive finite result can cover its explicitly proved domain. Neither automatically supplies external-system correspondence.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Test or otherwise substantiate a path, use rebuild, repair the missing resource or accept loss.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CHEAP_PATH: Rebuild reproducible stateless assets and perform a direct function check.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: C04'sinternalrestorationcanholdwhilecredentialandexternalconditionsfail; an encrypted backup without its lost key does not satisfy even the internal restore requirement.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.EXPIRY_OR_FRESHNESS: Reassess evidence when a relevant configuration, profile, environment, support or dependency change alters a premise. No arbitrary periodic expiry or full-retest rule follows for unaffected claims.
RELIABILITY_EVIDENCE_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: Backup existence does not entail that required data or function can be recovered under the relevant loss scenario. Guard: The invalid implication is rejected. A backup can be valuable evidence of stored state, and a bounded restore demonstration can establish more without proving every disaster.

current_claim.bearer: One finite failover exercise and a broader disaster-recovery claim.
current_claim.proposition: A failover result supports the conditions and faults it actually challenges; it does not by itself establish all disaster recovery paths.
current_claim.guard_quantifier: A single test can be sufficient for a narrow deterministic question. Generalization needs a justified fault/profile/configuration relationship, not an arbitrary larger test count.
current_claim.model_domain: An observed finite result is not a universal quantifier over untested faults.
current_claim.mechanism: Keeps test coverage, state, load and postconditions attached to the claim.
current_claim.consumer_decision: Retain the tested claim, narrow a broader one or test a material remaining difference.
current_claim.positive_scope: One adequate local test and carefully scoped broader exercises.
current_claim.negative_scope: Universal disaster-recovery inference rejected; no rule that every useful claim needs multiple exercises.
current_claim.counterexample: A stateless worker failover does not test a corrupt backup, stale authority or shared control-plane outage.
current_claim.criterion: Map the exercised fault and receiving predicate to the intended claim; identify the concrete untested discriminator.
current_claim.evidence_ceiling: Operator narrative and scoped experiment literature; native Meta2021postmortem is retained as historical cited evidence, not newly read testimony.
current_claim.remaining_premises: Representativeness, current state, dependencies, capacity and adequate observation.
current_claim.cheap_path_alternatives: Recheck the changed component/path or use existing valid evidence when it settles the question.
current_claim.cost_retirement: Full exercises can be expensive and disruptive; repeat only for a material uncertainty, invalidation or applicable obligation.
current_claim.audit_question: Which specific disaster difference is outside this exercise, and is a new test needed to resolve a real decision?
current_claim.change_note: Original rejection retained while protecting legitimate sufficiency of one narrow test.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RECOVERY_ACTION: Keeps test coverage, state, load and postconditions attached to the claim.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RPO_OR_STATE_LOSS_BOUND: State/data loss bound where the function depends on preserved state; explicitly state a nontrigger for stateless or directly reconstructible functions.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RTO_OR_RESTORATION_BOUND: The declared restoration interval or bound, if the claim requires one. Distinguish detection, waiting, logistics, repair and validation and avoid summing overlapping intervals.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.STATE_RECONCILIATION: Reconcile the state required by the named restored function. Broader divergent or external state may remain an explicit residual; authoritative wider service requires its own relevant conditions.

RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.DEPENDENCY_POSTCONDITIONS: Verify dependencies that the particular restoration claim requires. Record unverified external dependencies separately; they prevent an unsupported wider completion claim but do not erase a valid internal postcondition.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.VALIDATION: An observation or proof adequate to the named functional/state postcondition. Independent end-to-end checks are appropriate when the claim needs them, not a universal prerequisite for every local deterministic restoration.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.RETURN_TO_SERVICE_AUTHORITY: Keep proof of the postcondition separate from actual permission to resume consequential service. Name the relevant decision maker or rule when applicable.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.ROLLBACK_OR_FALLBACK: A justified bounded fallback where it adds protection. It need not resolve every root cause, and not every restoration claim requires a second full recovery mechanism.
RECOVERY_RESTORATION_PROFILE.MATURE_FORM: A failover result supports the conditions and faults it actually challenges; it does not by itself establish all disaster recovery paths.
